slicingContext: unity-demo/Build/webBuild.loader.js is a single top-level function declaration (createUnityInstance) covering the whole file — its slices descend one level into that function body and cut at ITS top-level statement boundaries; the wrapper head line, the final body-level `return` statement (a bare return is illegal outside a function) and the closing brace are skipped (index-only) sections
note: Ultimate Water 2D Web Demo (https://diffusionworks.com/web-demo) is capture-class: a route page of a closed product site wrapping a Unity WebGL build at /unity-demo/. §0.4 fork-over-mirror was checked on 2026-10-13 — the product site publishes deployments, not sources, and no public upstream repo exists for this demo (GitHub search finds only this mirror's own repo), so the mirror stands. SCOPE: the DEMO's closure only — the Nuxt shell bits needed to boot the demo page plus the Unity WebGL build; other site routes (docs/support/privacy/...) are deliberately not captured. Derived pipeline: capture → pinned prettier 3.9.6 (module API, default options, single pass verified idempotent — never the CLI: it respects .gitignore and can silently echo its input) → readable/<served path>.pretty.js|css per captured JS/CSS file; the capture preserves the served URL structure, so the derived layers MIRROR it — nested directories and the served filenames kept, no __ flattening (taipei-rush-tokyo precedent, PLAN §5); every pretty provably NOT byte-identical to its capture source. The Unity framework (unity-demo/Build/webBuild.framework.js.unityweb) is a gzip stream as served: it is decompressed IN MEMORY (never stored decompressed) and prettified to readable/unity-demo/Build/webBuild.framework.js.pretty.js. src/: statement-aligned slices of the demo's own glue — unity-demo/Build/webBuild.loader.js (the Unity loader: download, progress, in-JS gzip inflate of the .unityweb payloads) and _nuxt/B9hgXP_e.js (the /web-demo route component): top-level declaration boundaries only, ~250-350 line windows, oversized single declarations stay whole, exact 2-line provenance header, each slice parses standalone under `node --input-type=module --check -` and round-trips byte-exact to its recorded readable line range (through the recorded semantic rename map where one is recorded). Site-shell machinery rule — wholeFile sections, never sliced: _nuxt/l-4XETKm.js (Nuxt entry boot), _nuxt/A3EUxX58.js (Nuxt/Vue vendor bundle), _nuxt/Buq_OoVt.js, _nuxt/bBm2T0bl.js, _nuxt/c0TEtrJJ.js (Nuxt utilities/glue) and the Unity framework region — product-framework code, not demo code. Vendor payload rule — notRendered with bytes + sha256: webBuild.data.unityweb and webBuild.wasm.unityweb are UnityWeb gzip streams stored exactly as served (Unity's loader inflates them in JS; no Content-Encoding on the wire), plus the seven Inter woff2 subsets, every image/ico and the two recorded JSON build files. Inline scan: web-demo/index.html carries an importmap block (json twin), the __NUXT__ boot script (js twin) and a typed Nuxt data block (inline-data notRendered); unity-demo/index.html carries the Unity template boot script (js twin). Identifiers in src/ carry the semantic rename campaign (PLAN §5) to the extent the bytes allow: the app's own /web-demo Nuxt route component is renamed (tools/names.json -> tools/apply-names.mjs -> rename-map.json, recovered by tools/recover-scoped-map.mjs and re-applied here on every re-cut); the Unity loader is Unity's generated loader machinery whose whole body sits inside one top-level function declaration, so the campaign's program-scope rule cannot reach it and the vendor rule leaves it unrenamed (recorded honestly in README.md, not claimed). Capture bytes are untouched by everything above; re-cut with `node tools/derive.mjs` after any capture refresh. `node tools/audit.js` is the gate.

rename.pipeline: tools/names.json (reviewed worklist) → tools/apply-names.mjs (scope-aware writer, canonical guard family) → recovered by tools/recover-scoped-map.mjs
rename.note: Semantic renames are recorded per slice in rename-map.json and re-applied on every re-cut. The campaign covers the app's own /web-demo Nuxt route component only: its top-level compiler-generated bindings are renamed to reviewed semantic names. The Unity loader (unity-demo/Build/webBuild.loader.js) is Unity's generated loader machinery — its whole body sits inside one top-level function declaration (createUnityInstance), so the campaign's program-scope rule cannot reach it, and the vendor rule (deobfuscation applies to app code only) leaves it unrenamed; the site-shell machinery chunks and the Unity framework are wholeFile and never renamed.
